steps.text: Combine white sugar, brown sugar, flour, and cinnamon in a small saucepan. Stir in vanilla extract and water, then bring to a rolling boil over medium heat, stirring often. Continue to boil, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens to a syrup consistency, about 3 to 5 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool for 10 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Cinnamon Syrup
raw_recipe.description: This syrup is quick and easy to make and should keep you from having to run to the store on the morning you wake up wanting pancakes.
raw_recipe.name: Cinnamon Syrup

Continue to boil, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens to a syrup consistency, about 3 to 5 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool for 10 minutes before serving.

review.reviewBody: This is the first time I have ever had homemade syrup. We thought it was pretty good.I might even try adding a little butter next time.The first thing my 8 year old said was "that was awesome give me some more."It was a nice change from the same old boring maple syrup...since I doubled the recipe (to make sure there was plenty) I put the remaining syrup in an empty syrup bottle and placed it in the fridge. That seemed to work fine then you just microwave it for 10-20 seconds to warm it up the next time.

I took an extra step and added 1/2 cup chopped pecans that I had toasted in a frying pan with 1 tablespoon of butter... Yum! Gave a nice touch of crunch :) I didn't add the pecans until after the syrup had started to thicken slightly. My family loved it, too!

Excellent . No changes , except I used1 tbs flour and added 1 tabsp. of butter mixed in just before serving as others suggested. Husband said we don't need to buy anymore of that "store bought stuff ". Kiddos literally licked the plate. I made it 3 times because everyone wanted seconds and there were five eating. 

The last time I made it I used only brown sugar. Seemed even more smoother to me. I don't know why some said it was globby or crunchy. But it may have to do with temperature and cooking time. You will want to cook this over medium low to medium heat . Once you see it boil, turn it to medium low. Stir often. Thickens quick. Thickens more when cooling. 

Also, I used a fork to thoroughly wisk ingredients in pot before I began rolling boil. Hope this helps. This is an awesome recipe. Thanks for sharing .

The first time I made this, the syrup was decent but not great. The second time I made it, I scaled it to 6 servings and added a teaspoon of butter. That gave it a richer taste that was definitely better! Keep in mind that it will thicken as it cools, so stop cooking when it's still a little thin. If it coats the back of the spoon pretty well, it's probably ready.
Update: This is a good base recipe for lemon syrup! I used all white sugar, replaced half the water with lemon juice, and subbed lemon extract for vanilla. Delicious!

Maybe some of the "gloopy" results are that the recipe doesn't really state what temp the syrup should be cooked at. I cooked mine over medium, and turned off the heat as soon as the rolling boil covered the surface. It resulted in a really nice texture - not too thin or thick. I added about 1T of butter to finish it, and because it was so sweet I mixed in a couple pinches of salt which really woke up the flavor. This is definitely my go-to over store-bought, non-maple syrup. I will still reach for pure maple syrup for most stacks of pancakes, but this is a nice alternative, and would be extra good on pumpkin pancakes or french toast.

This syrup is absolutely delicious and comes together quickly. My niece and nephew devoured it on top of the recipe for good old fashioned pancakes also available from this site. The following are my notes to help troubleshoot some of the problems that others have reported: Once it reaches a hard boil, it takes less than a minute to be done. Remove from heat and rest for 10 minutes and it will be more of a syrup consistency and you won’t have the graininess that some have described. If will be the true pancake syrup consistency and will drizzle easily. If yours does not do this, you took the syrup too far and let it boil too long and started making candy. Not the recipe’s fault. You can still use it but you may have to smear it instead of drizzle it. This is a very flavorful syrup so if you think that it is bland, check the date on your cinnamon. While spices may not “go bad” they do lose potency so you may just need to use more. Hope that these tips help the original commenters and also encourage others that they can make a perfect syrup with this recipe.

I gave this four stars only because I tried some of the suggestions that others mentioned. Instead of flour I used 2 Tbls of corn starch mixed with 2Tbls cold water and added during the boiling point. I also added about 1 Tbls butter at the very end. It was very delicious.

Ever tried Starbucks Caramel Apple Cider? This is part of the recipe! Just buy freshly pressed Apple cider, normally located in your produce department. Make this recipe, mix it into your Apple cider and add a little Salted Caramel coffee syrup, heat to your desired degree, top with whipped cream and wah-la. Its great to mix altogether in the crock pot on high with a few cinnamon sticks for a fall or winter gathering. Want to spike it? Add caramel vodka ;-).

Just ran out of a bottle of brand named syrup and decided to not waste my money on something that is rather sweet but still tasteless.

This syrup is awesome on ANYTHING. I'm planning on making it for my daycare since I can use it without kids being allergic to it. I kept the old syrup bottle and doubled the recipe, exactly 750mL's. I DID use cornstarch instead of flour and I added at the end 2 tbsp of butter to deepen the color and it became even better.

wanted French toast, but had no syrup. found this and had all the needed ingredients. I did alter a little. some complaints were it was too thick. I added a couple tablespoons of milk, cut the flour to 1 1/2 tablespoon and put a tablespoon of butter in. it became really smooth. even when cold it is the perfect syrup consistency. we put it on top of vanilla ice cream for dessert. we are all hooked.

I subsitute 1/2 cup of brown sugar for 1/2 cup of white sugar to get more of the flavor out of the brown sugar while still using white sugar. The syrup is a little goopy but tastes phenomenal. If you're a heavy flavor person, you're going to want to add a looooot more cinnamon. I also added a sprinkling of clove and ginger to mine but that's my own personal preference. It came out wonderful and I poured it over sweet potatoes waffles!
This recipe is so easy to make! And it's delicious too!
Made this exactly as written and it was delicious! Will no longer be buying syrup at the store.
Thank you! I needed syrup in a pinch and this worked perfectly! You barely miss the maple flavor too.
This is my 2nd time making it. It's really easy and does the trick with pancakes.
Turn out great just added a little butter to remove the goopy consistency.
Delish over pumpkin pancakes, maybe a little less flour so it’s thinner? Added 2tb butter at the end and a little salt
This is the first time I made homemade syrup. Thought it was very easy to make and very delicious!!
It was so delicious. I made it for my family several times. It is really good with whipped cream on pancakes too! Try this recipe! It’s really good!
